messages:
ali: hey folks, accepted the org invite but I still get a 403 when trying to access private repos or re-run CI jobs. :confused:
marco: @ali which GH account did you accept with? personal or your work address?
ali: i used my work account (ali.codes@gmail.com) — weird thing is my commits on the fork show a different email (ali.dev@proton.me) in the commit metadata.
onboard-sre: that could do it. Our SSO mapping matches the verified work email attribute from the IdP to a verified email on the GitHub account. If the commit email is different it doesn't remove access, but if you have multiple GH accounts the PR owner might not be the SSO-mapped identity.
ali: actions shows: `403 Forbidden — You do not have permission to rerun this workflow.` and when I open the repo it says 'Access denied'.
it-bot: reminder: Redwood enforces SSO + 2FA for org resources. Make sure your GitHub account has a verified work email and TOTP enabled. Docs: https://redwood.dev/onboard/github
marco: quick checklist @ali: 1) confirm ali.codes@gmail.com has ali@redwood.ai as a verified email, 2) enable TOTP 2FA, 3) check if you have a second GH account (ali.dev@...) that actually owns the fork/PR.
ali: i do have another GH account (ali.dev). the fork/PR are under ali.dev. i thought since my work account is a collaborator it would be fine.
onboard-sre: forks are owned by the account that created them. SSO blocks access to private org repos for non-SSO-mapped identities. Two options: map the ali.dev account to SSO by adding ali@redwood.ai there (recommended if you want to keep PR ownership), or we can transfer the branch/PR to the SSO account but that may change author attribution in some UIs.
ali: i'd prefer to keep the PR under ali.dev if possible. can i add the work email to ali.dev and then accept SSO?
marco: yes — add ali@redwood.ai to Settings > Emails on the ali.dev account, verify it, then enable TOTP. Post here when done and i'll run a manual mapping sync.
ali: added the work email to ali.dev and enabled TOTP. clicked the org authorize link and it still shows 'pending' though.
onboard-sre: sometimes the mapping doesn't trigger automatically if you have two accounts with similar usernames. i ran a manual identity sync and pushed ali.dev into teams: eng, dev-tools. also temporarily granted write on repo "sdk" so you can re-run CI.
onboard-sre: sync complete. check Actions and repo now.
ali: re-ran the workflow and it accepted! PR and fork show up under the org now :tada:
marco: nice. FYI if you'd like to consolidate down to one GH identity later we can migrate forks/archives; but mapping kept your original author and commit history intact which is usually what folks want.
ali: huge thanks. one follow-up — my local git commits show the personal email in author lines. do i need to update them?
onboard-sre: not required for CI access. If you prefer consistency you can rewrite authors with git-filter-repo or use `git commit --amend --reset-author` on open branches, but we usually only recommend that for small fixups.
ali: got it. i'll keep as-is for now. thanks everyone — i'll drop an intro in #new-hires-intros and add my SSH key to the SSO-linked account.
it-bot: protip: use separate SSH keys per GH account to avoid duplicate-key rejection. See https://redwood.dev/onboard/ssh
